## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), \(J_v\subseteq H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) is generated by either Schur interval, each of cardinality \(\binom{a+b}{a}\). [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [source-backed] For a graded connected algebra \(\Lambda\) over \(R\), homogeneous generators of \(M\) are inclusion-minimal exactly when their images minimally span \(M/\Lambda_+M\); the paper specializes this with \(R=\mathbb Z\), \(\Lambda\) the symmetric functions, and \(M=J_v\). [source-2, lines 1520-1540]
- [proved] Let \((P)\) be the accepted exact integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation. Every non-source hypothesis used in the conditional \(a=1,b=2\) argument is a clause of \((P)\): integral graded Schur bases for \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) and \(J_v\), exact degreewise Schur-column lists in the \(q^r\)-box, and integral Pieri multiplication whose positive-degree product lattice is \(A_+J_v\).
- [proved] Under \((P)\), \(a=1,b=2\) implies
  \[
  i,j\ge2,\quad p:=q-i\ge1,\quad c:=r-j\ge1,\quad
  \min(i,j)=2,\quad\min(p,c)=1.
  \]
  Hence \(q,r\ge3\), and exactly the cases \(p=1,c\ge2\), \(p\ge2,c=1\), and \(p=c=1\) occur.
- [proved] Under \((P)\), with \(d=ij\),
  \[
  Q_d=\mathbb Z\bar x_0,\qquad Q_{d+1}=\mathbb Z\bar x_1,\qquad
  Q_{d+2}=\mathbb Z\bar x_2,
  \]
  where
  \[
  x_0=s_{i^j},\quad x_1=s_{(i+1,i^{j-1})},\quad
  x_2=s_{((i+1)^2,i^{j-2})},
  \]
  and \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1,\ \bar y_2=\bar x_2\), for
  \[
  y_1=s_{(i^j,1)},\qquad y_2=s_{(i^j,2)}.
  \]
- [proved] Under \((P)\), source-backed generation by \((x_0,x_1,x_2)\) induces a graded surjection
  \[
  \mathbb Zx_0\oplus\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\twoheadrightarrow
  Q:=J_v/A_+J_v.
  \]
  The preceding degreewise isomorphisms annihilate its homogeneous kernel, so
  \[
  Q\cong\mathbb Z^3.
  \]
- [proved] The two source-backed \(a=1,b=2\) generating families
  \[
  F_1=(x_0,x_1,x_2),\qquad F_2=(x_0,y_1,y_2)
  \]
  map to bases of \(Q\), related by \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)\). Therefore both are inclusion-minimal.
- [proved] **Target established internally:** the conditional qualification may be removed from the project-internal \(a=1,b=2\) conclusion, since all of its presentation hypotheses are supplied by the accepted exact integral presentation \((P)\). It cannot be removed in a standalone source-backed formulation from the supplied excerpts, which do not themselves state \((P)\).

## Strategy
Write the exact dependencies as follows.

1. From \((P)\), \(J_k=0\) for \(k<d\), while
   \[
   J_{d+1}=\mathbb Zx_1\oplus\mathbb Zy_1
   \]
   and
   \[
   J_{d+2}=\mathbb Zu\oplus\mathbb Zx_2\oplus\mathbb Zz
   \oplus\mathbb Zy_2\oplus\mathbb Zw,
   \]
   deleting \(u=s_{(i+2,i^{j-1})}\) if \(p=1\), and
   \(w=s_{(i^j,1,1)}\) if \(c=1\).

2. Since \(q,r\ge3\),
   \[
   (A_+J)_{d+1}=A_1J_d,\qquad
   (A_+J)_{d+2}=A_2J_d+A_1J_{d+1},
   \]
   with \(A_1=\mathbb Zh_1\) and \(A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2\).
   Integral Pieri gives the complete row systems
   \[
   h_1x_0=x_1+y_1,
   \]
   \[
   h_2x_0=u+z+y_2,\quad
   h_1x_1=u+x_2+z,\quad
   h_1y_1=z+y_2+w.
   \]
   Also \(h_1^2x_0=h_1x_1+h_1y_1\), so these rows span the whole product lattice.

3. In degree \(d+2\), retaining \(x_2\), the complementary minors are unimodular:
   \[
   p=1,\ c\ge2:\quad
   \det\!\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\1&0&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}=-1;
   \]
   \[
   p\ge2,\ c=1:\quad
   \det\!\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{pmatrix}=1;
   \]
   \[
   p=c=1:\quad
   \det\!\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}=-1.
   \]
   This proves the three displayed quotient components integrally.

4. The first source interval specializes to \(F_1\); its ideal generation gives the graded surjection to \(Q\). Since its source is supported only in degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\), the integral calculations in those degrees prove injectivity. The second interval specializes to \(F_2\), and the displayed relations make its image another basis. Apply the cited graded Nakayama proposition.

## Gaps
